column4: text
The Achaemenids withdraw from the desert; no power polices the caravan routes
Aretas I is recorded at Petra as "king of the Nabatu, master of the water of Sela"
Obodas I takes Hegra: the kingdom's second capital
The Dedan settlement: Lihyan's wells go into the Hegra registry
The notables of Damascus admit a Nabataean governor
Aretas III turns back a Masri army at the Wadi al-Arish
The Arabic Ordinance: Arabic in the Nabataean chancery hand becomes the language of government
The Water Ordinance puts every registered well into the Well Rolls
The Covenant of the Wells is sworn at Hajr: the Nabataean unification
Aretas V annexes Gerrha on the Gulf
The War of the Two Capitals between Petra and Hegra
Himyar takes Najran and diverts the incense trade to the Red Sea
Rabbel V dies without an heir; the kingdom dissolves into the Petra and Hegra leagues
Islam emerges in the Hejaz among a literate trading people
The Abbasid caliphate: Baghdad becomes the largest city on the planet
The Saqaliba Revolt: European captives rise in the Basra marshes
The rebels sack Basra
An Abbasid army destroys the rebel capital after fourteen years
The sack of Baghdad; the Interregnum begins
Mansa Jata of Kaabu reaches Aden around the Horn
Jolofian cartographers name the whole landmass Arabia
The colonial trade in Europeans begins
Hindustan charters the Red Sea Company; a settlement at Jeddah
The Duala Company of Kamerun founds Magan Town
The Hassaniya crown settles the Tihamah coast
The Lakhnau Servitude Ordinance makes slavery hereditary
The Rashidi Wars begin
Najd, around Diriyah and Riyadh, becomes the thirteenth colony
The Jizan rising spreads along the Tihamah for three weeks
The Seven Years' War between Hindustan and Kong
Kong is expelled from the Euphrates
The Jeddah Coffee Protest
Fighting begins at Bab al-Hadid outside Aleppo
The Declaration of Independence
The Treaty of Zafar: independence; the frontier at the Euphrates
The Constitution in force; al-Hashimi is the first president
Hejaz cedes the federal district of Umm al-Qura
The Kuwait Purchase doubles the country
The import ban on enslaved people takes effect
The viceroyalty of Masr campaigns across eastern and southern Arabia
The War of 1812 with Hindustan
The Presidential House at Umm al-Qura is burned
The Euphrates Compromise; Jolof sells Magan
The Qasimi Doctrine closes the Arabian seas to new colonies
The Desert Removal Act: the Road of Thirst
The Republic of Sharqiyah
Sharqiyah and Magan join the Union
The Arabian-Masri War
The Treaty of Ras Musandam: Oman and Socotra ceded; pearls off Sur
Bleeding Shammar
Civil War: eleven states secede as the Islamic States of Arabia
The Manumission Proclamation
The last secessionist army surrenders at Wadi Hanifa
Adharbaijan is bought from the Abyssinian Empire
The compromise of 1877; the khidmah codes
The Trans-Arabian Railway is completed at Buraydah
Nsimba Malonga patents the motor carriage
The Gulf War with Jolof; Qumur is annexed
The partition of Europe is complete
The moving assembly line at Mosul
The First World War begins in Africa
Arabia enters the war
The Nineteenth Amendment: women win the vote
The Battle of Sabilla; the Jeddah Exchange collapses in October
Faisal ar-Rashid's New Awakening
Oil is struck at Dammam No. 7
Hindustan attacks the fleet at Yalang Yalang
The Alamut Project; the war ends; the Concert of Nations at Jeddah
The Umm al-Qura Pact; the Derg Union's first atomic test
The Bornean War
Adharbaijan and Qumur become states
The Year of Europe: seventeen states in twelve months
The Kartli Missile Crisis
The March on Umm al-Qura; President al-Sudairi is assassinated
The Thirty-First Amendment abolishes every remaining form of servitude
Hilal 11 lands on the Moon
The first oil shock
The siege of the Masjid al-Haram; the Adharbaijan hostage crisis
The Derg Union dissolves
The Jeddah World Trade Centre is destroyed
The financial crisis
Nusantara passes Arabia in purchasing-power output
The coronavirus pandemic
Munira al-Bahrani becomes the forty-seventh president
The reapportionment litigation
